reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio SAT2-SAT4 campus discloses 36 MW of IT capacity, but its certifications target regulated enterprise workloads, not the large AI clusters now driving data center demand.

The 36 MW across 295,785 square feet of technical space suggests the published figure captures the current footprint, not a future buildout. Certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942 qualify the campus for finance, healthcare, and federal computing, not for the large-scale AI training or inference deployments that drive recent data center demand.

Among Texas facilities, only 19 of 133 mapped sites publish capacity figures, and this campus ranks fourth by disclosed IT load, representing 7.6% of the state's published 475 MW. That rank reflects the scarcity of published specifications in Texas, not strategic importance to AI scaling. The site's power availability and grid constraints are not published, and its suitability score of 68 omits announced expansion, so the data cannot show whether this campus will grow with AI workloads.
